Bershad Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Bershad's Jews, present from the end of the 16th century, suffered under Cossack leader Maksym Kryvonis during the 1648 Khmelnytsky Uprising; the community was later influenced by Sabbateanism in the 17th century and became a center of Hasidism in the 18th. Bershad grew famous for its tallit-weaving industry in the early 19th century, and by 1897 numbered 6,600 of 8,885 residents, supporting eight synagogues and seven prayer houses by 1889. A ghetto established after the 1941 German-Romanian occupation held about 25,000 Jews deported from Bukovina and Bessarabia, with adult mortality reaching 50–70 percent; a Jewish underground resistance of 50 people later joined local partisans. This old cemetery, believed founded no later than the mid-18th century, holds a matzevah dated 1754.
